body.statement: For \(\Gamma_{k,m,M}\) with unit noncore weights and arbitrary positive integer core weights, the probability that every core vertex is selected is computable in \(O(k!km^2)\) rational operations and \(2^{O(k\log(k+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) bit operations. On a chamber ordered by \(\sigma\), put \(H_r=\sum_{i=1}^r h_{\ell,\sigma(i)}\), \(\beta_r=H_r+r(M+m)-1\), \(c_0=1/(k+1)\), and \(c_r=1/(r(r+1))\). The ordered-ratio integral is evaluated by \(V_1(q)=c_1^q\), \(V_j(r)=\sum_{q=0}^r\binom rq c_j^{r-q}V_{j-1}(q)/(\beta_{j-1}+jq+1)\), and \(I_\sigma=\sum_{q=0}^m\binom mq c_0^{m-q}V_k(q)/(\beta_k+(k+1)q+1)\).
body.justification: The recurrence demonstrates that exponentially dense conditional polynomials can still admit direct evaluated integration with only a linear moment index.
body.gap: Gamarnik--Goldberg obtain distributional bonus recursions for limiting weighted greedy performance, not this exact finite core-conditioned coefficient and its rational bit bound.
body.consumer: The recurrence is the technique donor and positive control for the heterogeneous moment-algebra construction.
